$comment: Base permission lists /port:init merges into a managed repository's .claude/settings.json.
A plugin cannot ship permission rules, so they must be installed into the repository itself.
The model is BROAD ALLOW, AUTHORITATIVE DENY. Stage agents do real work — install
packages, read CI logs, manage git in their worktree — so the allowlist grants
categories and the deny list draws the safety line. Deny beats allow at every scope.
Substitutions applied at install time:
{{integration}} / {{production}} — the protected branch name(s)
{{packageManager}}               — the repository's package manager binary, omitted if none
branches.production null means single-branch mode: /port:init drops the three
{{production}} deny entries below entirely, the same way it drops the
{{packageManager}} deny entries when there is no package manager — never left as an
unsubstituted placeholder.
Entries from the repository's extraAllow are appended to allow.
Rationale that must not be lost:
1. Edit(**) and Write(**) are REQUIRED, not convenience. Stage agents run
permissionMode: dontAsk, under which file edits are NOT auto-accepted and must be
explicitly allowlisted. The read-only agents keep disallowedTools: Edit instead.
2. Content emitters are deliberately ABSENT: echo, cat, head, tail, cut, diff, true.
Shell redirection cannot be denied by pattern — allow/deny matching operates on
parsed command tokens, while redirection operators are consumed by the shell and
never reach the compared string. So the allowlist itself is the control: a command
whose purpose is emitting bytes becomes a file-write primitive the moment a '>' is
appended. The commands that remain emit search results, paths, or metadata.
This NARROWS the bypass, it does not close it — `grep -v x f > f` still strips
lines, and Bash(git *) has always offered write primitives via git apply and
git checkout --. See PIPELINE.md, 'Known gap'.
3. Push-deny needs BOTH forms. The bare-branch form also catches --force and --delete;
the refspec form catches HEAD:branch, <sha>:branch, +HEAD:branch, and :branch.
Neither covers the other.
4. Read(~/.claude/plugins/**) is required, not convenience. Every stage agent is told to
read ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/PIPELINE.md for its operating rules, and the plugin's
installed location is outside the project. Without this, that read prompts in default
mode and is AUTO-DENIED under dontAsk — so agents would be instructed to read a file
they cannot open, silently, looking like agents that ignored their own rules.
The '~/' form matters: this file is committed and travels into worktrees, so an
absolute path would break for anyone else who cloned the repository.
Read only. Never grant Edit or Write there — an agent must not be able to rewrite the
instructions it is running under.
5. find needs its no-leading-path forms too. GNU find defaults to searching '.' when
given no path, so `find -delete` has no token between 'find' and the flag for a
leading-argument pattern to match. Without these, the broad find allow becomes an
rm-equivalent escape hatch.
This file is public. Nothing secret may ever live here.
